column1: # PROVENANCE of the pre-push files this repo VENDORS from omnibase_infra
# (OMN-17435). Read by tests/scripts/test_prepush_host_table.py.
# WHY VENDORED AND NOT SHARED -- the decision, on the facts, not on preference:
#   * A sibling-clone source (`. "$OMNI_HOME/omnibase_infra/scripts/hooks/..."`)
#     makes a FAIL-CLOSED gate depend on a second repository being checked out
#     next to this one. An isolated single-repo clone, a CI runner checkout, or
#     a contributor without the whole workspace would then hit `die` on every
#     heavy push. A placement optimisation must not be able to brick a push.
#   * A pip-installed picker moves the gate behind a synced `.venv`, which a
#     pre-push hook cannot assume exists -- and the hook must run BEFORE the
#     machinery that would install it.
#   * A git submodule has the same failure shape as the sibling clone, one
#     `git clone` flag away (`--recurse-submodules` omitted -> empty dir).
# So the copy is local, and the DRIFT is what gets mechanically controlled:
# each file's sha256 is pinned, and the upstream revision it was taken from is
# recorded HERE so "has upstream moved?" is answerable by anyone with network
# access, without this repo depending on that access at push time.
# WHAT THIS FILE ADDS OVER A BARE DIGEST PIN (the OMN-17159 shape): a digest
# alone detects a LOCAL edit. It cannot tell you the copy is STALE. Measured
# 2026-09-01, that is not hypothetical: omnibase_core's OMN-17159 copy pins
# 067706bb...c096 = omnibase_infra commit 81955c0d0 (OMN-17269), while
# omnibase_infra dev already shipped 3e1c975b0 (OMN-17392, memory-aware
# admission + prefer_remote + bounded off-box wait) as ba56bd0d...9f88. Core's
# vendored copy was a full feature behind before its own PR merged. This repo
# therefore vendors the CURRENT tip and records which commit that was.
# TO UPDATE: re-copy the file from the named upstream path, update BOTH the
# sha256 and the upstream_commit here in the same commit, re-run
# tests/scripts/test_prepush_host_table.py, and name the upstream revision in
# the PR body. Editing a vendored file WITHOUT touching this record is the
# thing that cannot happen quietly.
# 2026-09-04, OMN-17753 -- THE RE-SYNC CONDITION IS MET AND THE NOTES ARE
# COLLAPSED. This copy is now a VERBATIM re-take of upstream's file, not a
# cherry-pick, and it carries ZERO executable deltas ahead of omnibase_infra
# dev for the first time since 2026-09-02.
# WHAT RETIRED THE LAST DELTA. The OMN-17606 slot-probe fix -- which omnimarket
# landed FIRST (#2276) and upstream did not yet have, the one reason a verbatim
# re-take would have REGRESSED a landed fix -- merged upstream as `8b8fd8966`
# (#3167). It is an ancestor of the commit pinned below, so the delta the
# OMN-17606 / OMN-17564 / OMN-17726 notes tracked is now simply IN upstream.
# Those three notes are deleted rather than kept: their whole content was the
# arithmetic of a divergence that no longer exists, and the history they record
# is `git log` of this file.
# WHAT THIS RE-TAKE ADDS, both landed upstream since the previous pin
#   * OMN-17741 (`4053dc3c0`, #3161) -- the wrapper CONSTRUCTS a registry root
#     on the target host and exports OMNI_HOME to it. `ssh` forwards no
#     environment, so every dispatched suite previously ran with OMNI_HOME
#     unset and fell back onto a home-relative default that exists on the lab
#     Macs and is TCC-denied to `sshd`. The repo name travels as a TENTH
#     positional; this repo's own tests pad it (see `_run_wrapper`).
#   * OMN-17787 (`812d0b545`, #3179) -- the collected count is read from a
#     `--junitxml` report instead of a banner `pytest-xdist` no longer prints,
#     and a count of ZERO on a green exit is now NO EVIDENCE (rc 1) rather than
#     an accepted PASS.
# THE SECOND ONE IS WHY THIS RE-VENDOR IS NOT ROUTINE MAINTENANCE. The
# reproduction that surfaced it was a push from THIS repo. Branch
# `jonah/omn-17774-g3-sessions-busback`, two governed pushes on 2026-09-04 --
# (`565a236a36f6dc3721a7e8b81727ef4d2d6006ae`) -- each selected
# `is_full_suite=True reason=changed_test_unnarrowable paths=[tests/]`, the
# heaviest escalation the selector can order, dispatched to h201.2, and were
# each answered "REMOTE LAB RUN PASS accepted in place of heavy fail-closed
# full-suite escalation: h201.2 ran 0 tests green" and then "SKIPPING the local
# full suite". The zero did not merely mis-log: it SATISFIED the escalation and
# suppressed the local full suite. Every push from this repo carried that hole
# until this row moved.
# BYTES: differ from upstream `812d0b545` by COMMENT WORDING ONLY, in five
# passages, for the reason the deleted notes already recorded -- upstream's
# prose names a vendoring repo by name, and
# `test_the_picker_library_is_not_edited_into_a_repo_specific_fork` forbids
# that token inside the shared library here, so the same facts are stated
# repo-neutrally. NO EXECUTABLE LINE DIFFERS: verified by stripping comments
# and blank lines from both files and diffing -- 925 executable lines each,
# empty diff, with a positive control (the same stripper against the PREVIOUS
# vendored copy) returning a 37-line diff.
# RE-SYNC CONDITION: there is no outstanding delta, so the next update is a
# plain verbatim re-take whenever upstream moves. Re-copy the file, update BOTH
# fields in the row below, and re-run tests/scripts/test_prepush_host_table.py
# plus tests/scripts/test_prepush_remote_leg_policy.py. If upstream's wording
# still names a repo at that point, the fork guard is the authority -- raise it
# upstream, never silence the guard to make the digests match.
#path
scripts/hooks/prepush_dispatch.sh
scripts/hooks/prepush_override_grant.py
scripts/hooks/pytest_full_suite_host_guard.py
